name: Ju
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1, languoid juuu1243 'Ju' (HTML page and JSON record), plus reference records 76828 and 569683 and the pages for guru1272, tala1296, sout3161, tala1295, zang1255, kirb1236, mang1416.
sources.note: Bibliographic only: the two Glottolog's most extensive descriptions for Ju are both 'a wordlist or less' (Decker et al. 2022; Shimizu 1978); the Guruntumic, Tala-Sho-Zangwal and South Bauchi East group pages cite only Shimizu 1978; no grammar, sketch or phonology exists for Ju in Glottolog.
Nothing; cites only Ethnologue 25, Blench 2006 AALIST, Blench 2012 Atlas, Blench 2021 West Chadic classification, OLAC and Glottolog. Notes 'The language is unwritten.'

sources.note: Nothing. Sections 8.3 'Phonetic inventories' (consonants, 5-8 vowel system, vowel length) and 8.5.1 'Phonological variation between Juu, Tala, and Zamwar' (pp. 28-30: b~p, d~t, g~k, final ŋ~n, final i~Ø correspondences) contain no prosodic statement; the word 'stress' does not occur in the document. Appendix F (p. 49) says the 222-item wordlists (Bauchi Juu, Dass Juu) are preliminary 'since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features'; entries carry pitch diacritics but no tone or stress analysis. sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2021. The South Bauchi languages: Nigeria's largest group of (almost) unknown languages. Unpublished paper (write-up of the CALL 2020 talk), posted on academia.edu (item 60223782), announced in Chadic Newsletter Online, 30 October 2021.
sources.note: Group-level only: South Bauchi languages have three level tones (H/M/L) or two (H/L) plus downstep, some with glides; Ju (Sho) is listed but its own tone system is not stated.

tone.quote: S. Bauchi languages: tones SB languages have either three tone (H/M/L) or two (H/L) plus downstep Some languages have glide tones (falling / rising), but elsewhere they seem to be largely absent Provisional prediction is that PSB had three tone levels (like much of neighbouring A3 for example) but is in the process of reducing to two in some languages
